transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because I just can't seem to shake this feeling lately. It's... just a heavy mix of fear and guilt, I suppose. 

I'm just tense all day, kind of waiting for something else to go wrong. And... I don't know, I just keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened. That's... pretty much it.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you can't get out of your head?

Um... yeah, I guess. Mostly when I'm working. I'll just be... I don't know, measuring a railing, or... I'll hear a ladder scrape somewhere. And then out of nowhere, I just... I see my husband falling. 

It's like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just drops and my hands get kind of shaky. So... yeah. I guess I do.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of fear and guilt?
Um... about four months. Ever since... well, we were repairing the porch and he fell. So, just since then.
Are there any specific things, like places or objects, that make you think of your husband's fall and trigger these feelings?

Um... I guess so. Raised porches, mostly. Or... second-story decks. I've actually kind of been turning down those jobs lately. 

And at home... I don't know, I just try not to look at the spot where it happened. If the repair comes up, I usually just find an excuse to go do something else. I just... don't really want to talk about it.
Are there any activities or things that you're avoiding because they remind you of your husband's fall?

Um... well, like I was just saying... it's mostly those specific jobs. The raised porches and the second-story decks. I just turn them down now. 

And... yeah, at home, I just stay away from that spot. If someone brings up the repair, I just find an excuse to leave the room. I just... really try to avoid it.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the moment of your husband's fall, like you're back in that moment?

Um... sometimes, yeah. Like... if I'm at work measuring a railing, or... if I just hear a ladder scrape. It kind of happens out of nowhere. I just... I see him falling, like it's happening right in front of me again. My stomach drops, and... my hands get kind of shaky. So... yeah. I guess I do.
Are there any other activities, besides work or being at home near the spot where it happened, that you avoid because they remind you of your husband's fall?
Um... no. Not really. Just... what I already told you. I don't think there's anything else.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?
Um... no. Not really. I still do... the normal stuff I usually do. I haven't really noticed anything like that.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, when you're reminded of your husband's fall?
Um... no. I don't... I don't think so. I'm just... I'm there. I don't feel like I'm watching it from the outside or anything.
Do you find yourself jumping or startled more easily than you used to, even by small things that wouldn't have bothered you before?
No, I don't think so. I mean, loud noises might make anyone jump, but... I haven't noticed it being any worse than normal.
Have you noticed any decrease in interest in activities that were important to you before your husband's fall?
I think you just asked me about that... but, no. Like I said, I still do the same things. Nothing's really changed there.
Have you noticed yourself pulling back from social interactions or hobbies since your husband's fall?
I... no. Not really. Um... I still see people. Like I was saying, I just do my normal stuff. Everything is mostly the same.
Have you noticed any changes in how much you want to participate in things you normally do since your husband's fall?
I... I feel like you keep asking me the same thing. Um. No. Like I said before, I still do my normal stuff. There's really no change.
Have you felt less interested in things you used to care about since your husband's fall?
I... look, I don't really know how many different ways I can answer that. It's still no. I care about the same things I always have.
Have you felt less interested in social activities since your husband's fall?
I... I don't know why we're still talking about this. No. I haven't. I'm just... I'm doing what I always do.
Do you try to push away or avoid feelings related to your husband's fall?

Um... I guess so. I mean... I don't really want to think about it. I've been... at work, I've been turning down inspections if they have raised porches or second-story decks. And at home... I just find things to do so we don't have to talk about fixing it. I don't really want to look at the spot where it happened.
Have you felt less interested in things you used to enjoy doing since your husband's fall?
I thought you just asked me that. No, I haven't. I still enjoy the same things.
